newsitem.title: UK: NatWest '97 forecasts seen largely unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NatWest '97 forecasts seen largely unchanged.

text.p: Analysts were not expected to revise their 1997 profit forecasts for National Westminster Bank Plc after the bank met with analysts on Tuesday.
Earlier, NatWest posted annual pre-tax operating profits of 1.12 billion stg.

While the figures were in broadly in line with market expectations, shares in the group tumbled 36p, or 4.4 percent, to 776-1/2 by 1331 GMT after the bank did not announce a share buy back and predicted slower economic growth in 1998 in the UK.
John Tyce, bank analyst with SocGen, said he raised his 1997 profit forecast by 50 million stg to 2.25 billion.
According to the Estimate Directory, analysts' estimates ranged between 1.8 billion and 2.3 billion stg, with the median at 2.07 billion.
Morgan Stanley bank analyst Nick Collier, said he was reviewing his estimates, but did not expect to revise them significantly.
Hugh Pye, banking analyst with BZW, said he also was looking at his numbers, but would make only marginal adjustments.
